name: Downtown and Channel District
tagline: Riverwalk towers and a walkable waterfront core
description: Tampa's centre pairs the 2.5-mile Riverwalk with the newer Water Street and Channel District blocks, where glass residential towers sit above ground-floor coffee shops and restaurants. It is the one part of Tampa built for pedestrians, with a free streetcar running east to Ybor and the hockey arena in the middle of it.
bestFor: Nomads who want to live without a car and work from waterfront cafes.
pros: Riverwalk plus the free TECO streetcar
Newest apartment stock in the city
Restaurants and gyms at street level
cons: Very quiet on weekends outside event nights
Low-lying and exposed in hurricane season

name: Hyde Park and SoHo
tagline: Bungalow streets, oak canopy and Bayshore Boulevard
description: South of downtown across the Hillsborough River, Hyde Park is Tampa's prettiest older neighbourhood: brick streets, restored bungalows and oaks draped in Spanish moss. Hyde Park Village handles the shopping, South Howard Avenue handles the bars, and Bayshore Boulevard gives you a long waterfront sidewalk for running.
bestFor: Nomads who will pay more for shade, sidewalks and a walk to dinner.
pros: One of the few genuinely walkable areas
cons: Expensive for what you get in square footage
SoHo bar noise on weekend nights
Bayshore side floods in storm surge

name: Ybor City
tagline: Cigar-factory brick, roosters and late nights
description: The old Cuban and Spanish cigar district still has its brick streets, wrought-iron balconies and red-brick factory buildings, several now converted to lofts and offices. Free-roaming chickens are protected residents. Seventh Avenue turns into the city's main bar strip after dark, and the streetcar reaches downtown in minutes.
bestFor: Nomads who want character and cheap loft space and can sleep through noise.
pros: Cheaper than downtown or Hyde Park
cons: Seventh Avenue is genuinely loud until 3am
Feels empty and less safe on weekday nights

name: Seminole Heights
tagline: Craft breweries and bungalows on the river bend
description: A stretch of 1920s bungalows along the Hillsborough River north of downtown, now Tampa's independent food and brewery belt. Florida Avenue and Nebraska Avenue carry most of the restaurants, rents run well below the waterfront, and river parks give you kayaking access a few blocks from home.
bestFor: Nomads wanting a real neighbourhood and good food without downtown prices.
pros: Best value housing close to the centre
cons: You will need a car for most errands
Little in the way of sidewalks on side streets

name: Westshore
tagline: Office parks, malls and a five-minute airport run
description: Tampa's business district west of downtown is built around two big malls and clusters of office towers, with newer apartment complexes filling the gaps. It is the practical choice: gyms, chain groceries and the airport all within minutes, plus the causeway to St Petersburg starting on your doorstep.
bestFor: Nomads who fly often and want new-build amenities over neighbourhood charm.
pros: Five to ten minutes from Tampa airport
Modern complexes with pools and gyms
Fast access to the bay bridges and beaches
cons: Heavy rush-hour traffic on Kennedy and Westshore
